findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: docs/host-run-usage.md:433 promises the serialized cap-lowering and corrupt-slot transaction cannot slip past the cap, and docs/host-run-usage.md:454 promises every live high-index slot is counted. However, packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:228 omits every fresh non-reclaimable corrupt slot from the live count, while packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:366 bases admission on that reduced count and packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:370 visits only indices below the lowered cap. An isolated source reproduction with cap=1 and a fresh corrupt slot-1 returned {"admitted":true,"allocated":"slot-0.json"}; an unknown high-index holder can therefore coexist with a newly admitted provider. The tests cover valid high-index lowering and expired low-index corruption separately but omit this fail-open combination. severity=critical

packages/main/src/tasks/managed-host-run-process-smoke.ts:121-138 asserts that a leaderless process group with a surviving child receives no TERM or KILL and remains unreaped, matching packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:2652-2655. This fail-closed behavior avoids a blind negative-PGID signal, but it directly contradicts the must-level CHK-003 edge intent at .lattice/story/actives/B-137a/checklist.json:516, which is marked done and requires the leader-exit case to escalate to KILL and reap. The recorded PASS selector therefore proves the opposite behavior instead of satisfying that intent. Reconcile the acceptance contract with the safety decision, or introduce a safe continuously bound descendant identity mechanism and a test that actually satisfies the stated intent. severity=high
